350-HP 2027 Chevrolet Colorado EPA Gas Mileage Ratings Are Now Live
66 photos
Photo: Chevrolet / EPA / edited
GM has found a few additional horsepower for the 2027 model year Colorado, but somebody checking the Monroney sticker won't find much reason to celebrate. Per the Environmental Protection Agency's published ratings, the mid-size pickup generally returns the same combined gas mileage as the 2026 model. Only a few changes between city and highway driving are worth your attention.
The worst offender here is the ZR2 with the Bison package, which drops to a thirsty 15 miles per gallon combined. Instead of the previous L3B version of the 2.7-liter turbocharged inline-four engine, 2027 models feature the L4B. Maximum output climbs from 310 to 350 horsepower, while peak torque is now listed as 450 pound-feet (610 Newton-meters) instead of 430 lb-ft (583 Nm).
How did General Motors do it? First and foremost, the Detroit-based automaker switched to a different turbocharger. Redesigned pistons also need highlighting, and updated fuel injection hardware seals the deal. As ever, prospective customers are presented with an eight-speed automatic transmission and either rear- or four-wheel drive.
There are two distinct 4WD transfer cases to speak of. The lesser unit is a two-speed affair, whereas the heavy-duty transfer case of the ZR2 was designed specifically for off-road shenanigans. Base 4WD trucks get open rear diffs that rely on StabiliTrak brake-actuated traction control to manage wheel spin. Higher up the spectrum, there's the G80 auto-locking rear diff and the ZR2's electronic push-button locker. The ZR2 also features a full-locking front diff.
Having cleared that up, it's worth remembering how the EPA actually measures gas mileage. The agency uses a five-cycle testing framework, covering heavy urban traffic, highway driving, higher-speed and more aggressive acceleration, cold-weather operation with the cabin heater running, and driving the vehicle with the AC on to measure the extra powertrain and battery load.
Photo: Chevrolet With that out of the way, the Colorado 2WD provides the least complicated direct comparison between the 2027 and 2026 model years. Now good for 20 mpg city, 24 mpg highway, and 21 mpg combined, the Colorado 2WD used to achieve 19 mpg city, 24 mpg highway, and 21 mpg combined. The combined figure can be read as 11.2 liters per 100 kilometers in metric lingo.
The base Colorado 4WD gets 19 mpg (12.4 l/100 km) in the combined test cycle, with the new truck improving city mileage by 1 mpg while sacrificing 2 mpg on the highway. Upgrading to the ZR2 gets you 1 less mpg in the city while leaving highway and combined efficiency untouched from 2026.
The ZR2 with the Bison package, however, loses 2 mpg highway and 1 mpg combined from its 2026 model year equivalent. Make that 6.7 gallons of dinosaur brew per 100 miles, namely 15.7 liters per 100 kilometers, making it the least economical configuration in the EPA's 2027 model year listings. Only the ZR2 Bison suffered a decline in combined EPA gas mileage.
Even so, the additional torque is a great trade-off as long as the ZR2 Bison is used extensively off the beaten path. Additional torque also comes in handy when towing. Chevrolet quotes up to 7,700 pounds (3,493 kilograms) for model year 2027, while payload tops 1,710 pounds (776 kilograms). In this regard, nothing has changed from the 2026 model year Colorado midsizer.
Via // EPA
